Success criteria: Both bottles must simultaneously remain suspended well above the table, with the red-capped bottle near the target slightly left of the centerline in front of the robot and the green bottle near the target slightly right of it. ## Execution tips

- Grasp a relatively straight section of each bottle near its label, with the pads on opposite sides. Avoid the sloped shoulders and raised ridges at the bottom of the green bottle to reduce slipping or rotation after grasping.
- Approach from an open side of each bottle facing the robot and adjust the gripper orientation where there is clearance, reducing contact with objects behind them such as the mouse or pen holder.
- Open slightly wider than the selected bottle section. Before closing, use different views to confirm the fingers are on opposite sides with sufficient contact depth, avoiding judging enclosure from image overlap alone.
- The two arms can handle the red-cap bottle currently on the left and the green bottle on the right separately. Leave clearance between both bottles and the grippers as they lift and move forward toward each other, avoiding collision near the centerline.
- During lifting, watch whether the bottle body slides down relative to the pads. If a regrasp is needed, first return the bottle to table support if possible, then adjust the grasp to avoid dropping it when released in midair.
